title: Primitive Recursiveness of the Bounded-Index Skipper
statement: The partial reader that takes a natural-number bound $n$ and a finite Boolean string, reads an initial block of ones terminated by a zero as a unary numeral, and returns the remaining suffix exactly when the numeral is less than $n$ is jointly primitive recursive in $n$ and the string.
replaced:
The two-argument skipping reader that, given a bound $n$ and a Boolean string,
consumes a unary-encoded index (a block of true bits closed by a false bit) and
returns the unconsumed suffix precisely when the index is smaller than $n$, is
primitive recursive jointly in $n$ and the string.
